title: Studying Soft-matter and Biological Systems over a Wide Length-scale from Nanometer and Micrometer Sizes at the Small-angle Neutron Diffractometer KWS-2
protocol: Disperse polystyrene spherical particles with different sizes in a water solution of 90% D2O and 10% H2O at a volume fraction of 1%.
Transfer six solutions of polystyrene particles in D2O/H2O to quartz cells using Pasteur pipettes.
Fill each quartz cell up to the neck with the respective solution.
Close the quartz cells with their stoppers.
Install the filled quartz cells into Al-cartridges of the sample holder.
Place each filled quartz cell in a cavity of the cartridge ensuring it entirely covers the window opening for neutrons.
Place correction and standard samples (empty quartz cell, boron-carbide plate, and Plexiglas plate) in additional locations on the cartridge.
Leave one location free for empty beam measurement.
Cover the cartridge with Cd-coated Al-cover plates using cap screws (M3x5).
Fix the cartridge on the Al-frame of the sample holder using special Al screws.
Adjust the length of the collimation nose to determine the necessary space at the sample position.
Select the appropriate configuration for the sample holder from stored configurations in the collimation nose control system.
Install the appropriate sample holder/sample environment on the sample stage using Allen screws (M6x40).
Close the motorized sliding lead door by using knobs on its outer side, keeping control knobs activated until the door reaches the end position.

Choose the adequate experimental configuration and mode for performing the investigation in a Q range that is appropriate for the length scale of the structures and the correlation effects revealed by the sample.
Check the dynamic range of the instrument.
Choose the adequate experimental configuration based on the estimated level of scattered intensity.
Optimize measurement time by considering the stability of the sample.
Select proper resolution based on the approximate polydispersity degree in size.
Enable wavelength resolution tuning as needed.
Prepare the measurement software for conducting and visualizing the experiment.
Start the measurement software by typing KWS2TC in a terminal window.
Activate the main menu using the KWS-2 instrument's control computer.
Select the Configuration function to activate the kws2-Configuration menu.
Fill the User data fields with User name, E-mail, First part of filename, and Measurement comment.
Save the user data configuration by clicking Save.
Select the Sample function to activate the Sample configuration menu.
Fill the Sample title, Sample beam window - Size, Sample thickness, and Comment for each sample.
Save each sample configuration after completing the definition.
Leave the menu by clicking Close.
Save all configurations under the File function in the Configuration menu.
Select the Definition function to activate the kws2 Definition menu.
Define the experimental setup and measurement program.
Select the Sample function to activate the Select Samples menu.
Choose twelve samples from the list of known samples and move them to the Selected Samples field.
Order the selected samples using the blue vertical arrows.
Check sample parameters and adjust name, thickness, and comment if necessary.
Leave the menu by clicking Save or Close.
Select the Detector function to activate the Definition of Measurements menu.
Choose Standard as the measurement type in the Measurement area.
Select the proper time unit for the measuring time in the End Conditions area.
Select the experimental setup and working mode by choosing values for wavelength (Selector field).
Set the detection distance (Detector Distance field) as appropriate.
Choose data acquisition mode (TOF field).
Define aimed wavelength resolution (DLambda/Lambda field).
Specify measurement time (Time field).
Configure lenses (Lenses field).
Determine collimation distance (Collimation Distance field).
Click the New button to fix and store the configuration in the lower table.
Define subsequent configurations and store them similarly until all are completed.
Hit Save or Close in the Definition of Measurements menu when setup adjustment is finished.
Sort the list of measurements according to the three loops shown at the bottom of the menu.
Remove undesired measurements by marking their line and clicking the "X" button.
Adjust measurement time for each measurement as needed.
Leave the menu with Save or Close and return to the kws2 Definition menu.
Close the kws2 Definition menu and return to the main menu.
Select the Control function in the main menu of the KWS2 measurement software.
Log in with the username and password provided by the instrument scientist and lock the session for script generation.
Press Start and answer questions about sample position door and beam-shutter status.
Enable visualization of current values during measurement (motor positions, component statuses, count rate, integral intensity evolution).
Select Current Values to monitor ongoing measurements.
Conduct measurements according to the defined measurement program.
Activate the Stop function when integral intensity is sufficient or if failures occur.
Generate the Logbook by clicking on the Print button under Loop Definitions option.
Select Live-Display in the main menu of the KWS2 measurement software.
Choose either GEDET or PSD at the Type screen for data visualization.
Select Display Mode as three-dimensional, two-dimensional, or one-dimensional mode.
Enter plot options and parameter values in Radial average options menu to present data as intensity versus Q.
Choose a TOF-channel to visualize data collected in TOF mode.
Start the data processing software by typing the qtiKWS command in a terminal window.
Choose the New Script option on the right side of the main interface.
Choose the DAN option in the upper functions menu to activate data analysis functions.
Select the KWS-2 instrument from Options on the right-side menu to activate data analysis mode for the KWS-2 using the main detector.
Define the folder where measured data files are located and where corrected data files will be stored.
Choose the Tools option and activate the Header(s) function on the right-side menu.
Generate an info-table containing the files to be processed by clicking the left set of green arrows on the Header(s) field.
Load the measured files by clicking the right set of green arrows on the Header(s) field and selecting the measured files.
Activate the Mask function in the right-side menu.
Generate the active mask that defines the area of the detector for data processing.
Enter values in the Edge and Beam-Stop fields to define the corners of the rectangular mask.
Activate the Sensitivity function in the right-side menu.
Enter run numbers for the measurements of the standard sample, empty beam, and blocked beam in the marked green fields.
Click on the set of green arrows next to the yellow field for calculating the transmission of the standard sample.
Generate and name the sensitivity matrix by selecting Calculate as New.
Visualize the generated matrix using plot functions in the lower menu.
Repeat this procedure for other configurations if necessary.
Activate the Data Processing function in the right-side menu.
Generate the correction and calibration table.
Generate the script table to correct, calibrate, and perform radial averaging of the data.
Define the number of conditions used in the experiment using the horizontal slider on the top of the right-side menu.
Fill the fields indicated with the yellow pencil by entering for each experimental condition the run numbers for the empty cell, blocked beam, and standard samples.
Enter the run numbers of measurements with strong forward scattering in the Center field.

Enter the run number of an empty beam in the EB field and select the corresponding experimental condition for the calculation of the transmission of samples by checking the box next to the Tr (Ec-to-EB) function.
Click each button indicated by a set of rotating green arrows on the vertical series of options in order to load the information needed for data processing from the defined files.
Load the information for calculating the transmission of the empty cell.
Click the head of each yellow column in order to define the column name.
Generate and name the table of the data files that will be processed by clicking the New button.
Load the data files that will be processed by clicking the Add button.
Calculate the transmission of each sample by clicking the Tr button indicated with the set of rotating green arrows under the Script-Table Tools area.
Check the results in the generated table.
Choose Project to save results as tables or matrices in the current qtiKWS session.
Click the I[x,y] button to perform correction and calibration of two-dimensional data.
Click the I(Q) button to perform correction, calibration, and radial averaging of the data.
Plot the results using the graphical functions under Graph.
Chose Tools in the right-side menu and activate the TOF|RT option to split data collected with the main detector into single files corresponding to each time channel.
Click the TOF :: Calculate Parameters function and load one file to extract information about the TOF conditions.
Load a file of interest measured in real-time or TOF modes using the TOF|RT :: Sum vs Number :: Read function to generate a sum-tof-file table.
Plot the integral intensity as a function of time channels from the sum-tof-file using the graphical options under Graph.
Define processing parameters in the fields of the TOF function.
Click the TOF|RT :: All Selected Steps :: Proceed button to load data files into single files for each time slot.
Generate files containing data measured in every time slot, stored in the location defined previously.
Analyze data with improved resolution corresponding to Δλ/λaimed using the chopper.
Select KWS2-HRD instrument from Options on the right-side menu of the main interface to activate high-resolution detector analysis mode for KWS-2 measurements.
Activate Mask function in the right-side menu and generate an active mask that defines the active area of the detector.
Choose the DANP option in the upper functions menu.
Select the ASCII.2D option from the right-side menu.
Activate the 2D Masking function to define a special sector on the detector for data analysis.
Introduce the beam-stop center in the field Center.
Select the mask matrix and the value 0 in Mask :: Conditions to neglect the outside area of the special mask.
Choose the angular sector and click the colored button on the right side of the sector fields.
Proceed with the data measured with the high resolution detector, as in steps 5.5 and 5.6.
Save the qtiKWS project using the save functions under the File option of the upper menu.
